part.Name: Description
part.Short: Road-worn and rumor-led, they carry everything they own: a bedroll, an empty skin, and the name of a place where thirst is shared.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Field mud has dried in the seams of practiced hands. Seed, stalk, and harvest are read here as a calendar rather than a guess.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Road dust lies in layers on a coat mended at a dozen fires. The way between water, shelter, and trouble has become a practiced thing.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Bit pouches click beneath a patched apron. Every broken hinge and quiet capacitor is inspected with the calm of somebody who expects it to answer.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A reed case, two registers, and an ear trained for the difference between a custom and an insult travel together.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Bandage rolls, bitter powders, and a bone saw are packed separately and checked twice. They have done this before, which matters more than saying so.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Road dust pales a robe kept by patient mending. The machine-prayers are a culture carried in the hands now, not an allegiance owed to anyone here.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A bedroll is lashed between twitching shoulders, and old tribeskin has been patched with cloth from half a dozen roads. A keen nose tests the settlement's smoke, stores, and strangers.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Dust of a dozen roads on their boots, and no bedroll unpacked. They are only stopping.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Road dust is worked into ceremonial folds. This traveller has come for a story and the place where it happened.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Carries themselves like someone with somewhere better to be, and one good reason not to be there yet.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A camelfolk merchant whose ledgers name roads beyond Qud. They have enough wares for another journey and are looking, improbably, for a door worth closing behind them.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A settlement chronicle shares this shelf with copied testimony, local disputes, and the keeper's corrections. Every bound record can be taken down and read.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Bound registers stand spine-out beside working copies. The keeper permits reading at the copy tables and can point to every disagreement between editions.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A figure of the founder keeps the watch over the rite ground, cut in the young city's own dressed stone. Its twin stands across the processional way.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A close-woven reed hamper keeps apple pips apart from watervine cuttings. Its slat marker names the field and season; construction leaves it empty.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A wide fired jar stands stoppered beside the smoke hearth. Leaf, salt, and spice go in only when somebody carries them here; the new jar begins empty.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Rush, cord, and a smoke-cured hide lid make a low cache for trail meat. The red binding marks food for the watch; the cache is empty until hunters fill it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A lidded timber bin bears two cut marks: crop and field. It is common storage, usable by hand and empty when the commons is raised.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The familiar spiral-borer silhouette is fixed inside a dressed-stone collar. It displays the work face and performs no autonomous digging.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A stone-lined furnace banked for supervised casting. It carries no charge sink, fluid line, or automatic product.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A piped hearth inside the stone fire hall, inert until the foundry's named operation is performed.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A broad shaping block kept clear beside the casting lane.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A press frame without liquid, enclosure, power transmission, or autonomous stroke. Foundry hands operate it only inside a receipted purpose operation.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A knee-high lip of bonded pebble and cement keeps carried soil on the terrace without barring the service walk.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A shallow runnel cut through low sandstone carries wash-water away from the slab. Boots cross it without climbing.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A bent metal rib describes part of the mirror-ring without closing its processional throat.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A low fret of riveted metal separates ceremonial layers while leaving the old processional route open.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A low seat dressed from one block, broad enough for a witness who means to stay until the answer is given.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A marble seat with its front edge polished by petitioners and its back left cold for ceremony.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Bent tubes and a riveted seat make a chair that can be scrubbed clean and cannot be mistaken for comfort.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A riveted frame holds a narrow sleeping sling clear of the service floor.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A narrow sling for an off-watch guard to sit or doze without turning a muster room into a household bed.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A broad stone slab dressed level and left bare for work that would scar timber.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A pale marble slab whose dressed edges turn a work surface into an assertion of office.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Shallow metal shelves hold sealed rolls and procedure books where damp hands cannot reach them.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A rust-chewed locker bolted beneath the bench. Its labelled drawers are real storage, but construction leaves them empty.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Recovered drawers and open relay housings line the gate route. The cabinets are usable storage, empty when commissioned, and low enough to pass.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A curiosity cabinet rebuilt from recovered plates and panes. Its open frame protects the relic without pretending to be the relic.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A mute assembly of rods, gauges, and severed contacts is fixed to a witness plinth. Whatever work it once performed is no longer possible.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Recovered sheets, hammered flat and riveted into a vessel. It begins empty and catches only what reaches it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A folded and welded basin with a clean lip, empty until a gutter, pipe, or careful hand fills it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A weighted reed hamper marks a handling station. Its lid is stitched shut; it stores and supplies nothing.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A weighted, sealed hamper extends the seed-house handling rows without storing or supplying seed.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A weighted practice jar fixes the drying-yard rhythm. Its stopper is sealed; it contains and supplies nothing.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A hide-bound dummy cache marks the trail muster. It cannot hold meat, create provisions, or be opened.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A weighted timber box extends the commons' labelled rows. Its lid is fixed and no seed exists inside.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A scarred low board gives hands a place to rehearse their order. It is bare and holds no stores.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A ring of cold stones shows the spacing of a working hearth. No fuel, flame, heat, or light belongs to it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Shallow slats demonstrate the order of a rack, but carry neither shelf inventory nor hidden stock.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Three blank brinestalk pegs mark hand, haft, and point. No cradle is fitted between them, so this drill frame neither resembles nor serves as an arms rack.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A low marked slab establishes a position in drill or witness work. It grants no seat or rite.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A cut-down regeneration-tank shell has both jacket and floor split open. Apprentices align rinse vessels beneath its ribs; the wreck itself cannot collect, contain, or supply liquid.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A narrow rail fixes the public edge of a practice court. It is a marker, not a usable seat.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A narrow strip of canvas is rolled around a marked slat and bound at both ends. It teaches the order of clean bedding but cannot be unfurled or slept on.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A salvaged lens and painted alignment mark teach service posture. No light, charge, power transmission, or storage survives in this practice fixture.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A small timber wheel, treadle, and spindle turn fibre by hand beneath the shade. It drives no mill and draws no power.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Two severed cable ends are fixed across a cork alignment strip where a metal body meets the charge-bay. These leads neither store nor supply charge; the rooted bay alone performs the work.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Weathered horn and hide cord bind a standing stone at the moot's edge. It marks the challenge ring and performs no rite on its own.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A strip of smoke-cured hide is laced to a forked staff and cut with one claimant's mark. It extends the moot's witness line without pretending to be another challenge post.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Bright fragments are wired around a fixed chrome shape and left deliberately unrepaired. It holds offerings but grants nothing.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Whitewashed timber and recovered metal make numbered rests for inspected arms. Construction leaves every rest empty.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A blackened stone pan holds cold ash in processional order. No coal burns here and no light issues from it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Bleached bone and cast-off chitin are laced across a dry-laid fieldstone spine. The stone is commissioned fabric; the remains are vowed here and carry no stock or salvage value.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A trained fruiting vine turns around a low timber frame. It gives shade and shape to the bower but carries no harvestable crop state.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A living trunk, mineral-bright beneath its bark, holds the bough-school's shade. Desks and lessons bend around it; nothing here cuts or commands it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A living crystal shoot was coaxed sideways, then upward, until bough joined bough around a teaching cell. It is wall, shade, and Chavvah's lesson in one growth.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Lashed poles and borrowed planks. Somebody's promise is being kept, plank by plank.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Casks in a cradle of watervine rope. The whole settlement is counted here, dram by dram.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Watervine trained up a frame of lashed poles, tended for its own sake now rather than the settlement's. Whoever lives here eats a little better for the bother.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Stretched hides scraped and staked to cure in the sun. The household has taken up tanning, and the smell has followed them home.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A cask of dreadroot and iron-salt liquor, stirred with a paddle gone the colour of the dye. What comes out of it rides with the caravans.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Scraped skins pinned flat under a weighted board until they lie true enough to write on. Somebody here reads, and somebody here teaches it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A tin-lined belly sunk to its rim in the earth. It makes nothing: what is in it was carried here in somebody's arms or run down a gutter from the works above. When it is full, the whole town sleeps easier; when it rings hollow, everyone hears it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A communal chest with a slatted lid, cool air moving through the gaps. What is put in here feeds the settlement, not just whoever finds it first.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A patch of turned earth, staked and weeded by hands that have somewhere else to be. What comes up depends on what the ground already knew how to grow, long before anyone asked it to.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Canvas over a brinestalk frame, pegged against a wind that has opinions. It is not much. It is up before dark, which is the whole argument for it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Four tents in a line with a woven brake along the weather side. Nobody calls this a house, and everybody sleeps better.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Posts, wattle, and a door that shuts. The first building here that will still be standing when the person who raised it is not.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The hut, and a swept square of packed earth outside it with a rope line and a stool. Where the work happens when the weather allows it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Fieldstone to the eaves, timber above, and a hearth that draws properly. Two families and a cat.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Three households around one square, and a well-worn argument about whose turn it is to sweep it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A whole street raised in one season, every door the same width. The masons stopped signing them halfway along.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Marble facing over honest stone, and a step nobody is allowed to sit on. Somebody of consequence is expected, and will not arrive until the plaster is dry.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A courtyard, a gate that closes, and a name cut over the arch. Whether the name deserves the arch is the kind of thing the chronicle argues about for a hundred years.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Four storeys around a shaded well, stairs on the outside, washing on every rail. A quarter of the city roofed in one go, and full before the scaffolding came down.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A shallow bed scraped level and flooded thin. The sun takes the water and leaves something worth raking up; what drips off the drying racks at dusk is worth more still.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Pans stepped down a slope so each one drinks the last one's leavings. Worked in shifts by people who stopped noticing the smell some time ago.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Stretched canvas, a gutter of split cane, and a cask underneath. Nothing falls here; what it catches is the night giving back what the day took, and it works best when the cold is worst.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A whole roofline turned to the purpose, gutters running to a sunken row of casks. On a cold clear night it fills faster than the settlement drinks.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Squat domes of dressed stone, windowed on every face so the air walks through them, ranked around a sunken basin. They are cold inside at dawn and the walls run with it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Rank on rank of them out past the wall, spaced by a mason who worked out how far apart they had to stand, and gutters cut between the ranks to bring it all downhill to one place.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Somebody followed a damp seam back into the rock and found the lichen it was coming off. The face is cased in stone now, with a lead gutter under it and a cask at the end of that, and one of them goes down twice a day to scrape the growth back off the cut.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A worked gallery along the whole wet seam, propped and drained, with taps every few paces and a walkway that stays slick no matter what is laid on it. The lichen is farmed now rather than fought.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A hall built around one cold face, shuttered by day and thrown open at dusk, with the whole roof turned to catching what the stone gives up. The keepers took a dead still apart to learn it and never put that one back together.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A stone lid over seven hundred drams and a hatch with a lock everybody has the key to. Cool enough down there to keep a body from going off, which has been tried.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Open water inside your own wall, lined with dressed stone and edged with a low kerb. Every dram in it was carried or channelled here by somebody; it is a held thing, not a found one. Children are told not to, and do anyway.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Cistern, court, and channel, all one thing, and a keeper whose entire trade is knowing which valve. It makes not one dram: everything that goes through it came off the works upcountry or out of somebody's arms. The founder was elsewhere the day it was finished, and the chronicle says so in both registers.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Staked rows, weeded on a rota, watered by whoever drew the short straw. It is somebody's whole day and it feeds nine.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Turned earth to the fence line, sown by everyone who could be spared and harvested the same way. For two weeks of the year the settlement does nothing else.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Rows to the edge of the claim, and a plough that took a season's salvage to put together. The chronicle dates the good years from here.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Raised on staddle stones with a lid that keeps the vermin honest. What is in here is the difference between a bad year and a bad story.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Fields to the fence line, a threshing floor swept between harvests, and a barn at the end of them with the year's account chalked on the door. Three people work it and a whole town eats out of it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The quarter the rest of the city eats out of: rows past the eye's patience, a mill with metal in its gearing, and granaries standing in a line with their own road to the doors. It is the only paved way in the city that goes nowhere but a barn.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A whetstone, a tar pot, and a bench somebody keeps tidy without ever having been asked to. The camp's entire industry, and not nothing.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A hearth, a hammer, and someone who walked a long way for the chance to swing it. The ring of it carries further than the wall does.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Banked overnight and never quite cold. Getting heat to stay put is harder than getting it to start, and this is the building that knows the difference.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Dressed stone carries the furnace heat away from a worked-metal striking floor. A casting anvil, empty quench basin, parts rack, and fixed light turn the old forge into a hall that can work after dark.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A pit, two trestles, and timber stacked in ranks to season. One of them stands in the hole all day and gets the worse half of it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Bankers, chisels, and a spoil heap that grows all summer. The heap is half of every block the settlement builds with.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A furnace, a crucible, and somebody who can read the colour of the melt. Getting scrap back to liquid is the easy half.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Two stones and a long handle, and a fine grey dust on everything within ten paces. Turns a harvest into something that keeps.

part.Name: Mill
part.Transformations: Vinewafer,Starapple,Plump Mushroom,Bundle of Noisegrass,Godshroom Cap:r_KingdomGodshroomPickle,Dreadroot Tuber:r_KingdomDreadrootMash

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Benches down both walls, everything hung where it belongs, and three people who can tell you why. Half the settlement's cleverness lives in this room.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Long benches, a high seat nobody sits in, and the charter nailed where the light falls on it. Read out loud once a season whether anyone asks for it or not.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Earth trodden into a ring by everyone who has come here to drink, and the basin standing in the middle of it. This is the ground the first water was poured on, and nothing raised here afterwards will move it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A kerb of dressed stone laid in courses around the rite ground, wide enough to sit on and worn smooth where people do. The basin stands on the stone now. There is a queue at dusk.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Beams raised over the waterstone, so the kerb became the floor and the queue got a roof. The charter is read out loud in here; the arguing is done in the yard, under the awnings, where it can be heard.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A colonnade of shaped stone closed around the moot hall, which stands inside it yet, beams and all. The cairns line the walk where they already stood, the kerb is underfoot, and the basin is in the middle of everything, exactly where it was set down.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The basin the first water was poured from, set down where it was emptied and never taken up again. Whatever the settlement raises here is raised around it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A stake driven at the corner of a rectangle nobody has drawn yet. The founder paced this out on the day the first water was poured: it is the whole ground the heart of this place may one day take. Building inside it is allowed, and what you build there is marked to yield.

part.Name: Chat
part.Says: [a corner, and a pace-count cut into the wood.]

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Awnings, argument, and somebody's cousin selling salt at a price that is frankly insulting. Caravans stop here because it is worth stopping.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Hot stone, cold water, and the extravagance of spending either on being clean. Word of it travels further than word of the wall ever did.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A low wall around the stone and a gate left open on purpose. Whatever is poured here is still gone by morning.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Raised to be seen from the road, and sited so that the road has to look. What is worshipped in it is the settlement's own business, and has changed at least once.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Two registers of the same year kept on the same shelf, and a keeper who will show you both and let you decide. The disagreements are indexed.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A settlement-made frontier gate with two watch seats set beyond its guarded throat. Its exact fabric answers the place that raised it, and its open centerline remains the way through.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The watch sleeps in shifts and eats together, which is why the watch is a thing and not a rota. Boots by the door in the order they came off.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Two bunks face a warm common room. The muster is kept beside the only outer door, where the watch can answer the wall without pretending this house is itself a fortification.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A stake driven into the ground, and a promise nailed to it: something is meant to rise here, as soon as the water and the hands can be spared.

part.Name: Chat
part.Says: [a design, chalked hastily beneath the notice.]

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Cord and pegs marking out a rectangle of ground, and a tally of days scratched into the corner post. Something is being made here, a stage at a time.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A load-bearing cradle of lashed poles, numbered joints, and chalked object tallies. The old lot remains standing until this exact frame is ready to receive it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A numbered corner stake joined to the moving frame by taut cord. It reserves only the exact destination named on the ring-call slate.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A squared post sunk into cleared ground, waiting for a wall to be built against it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Rope-sprung and blanket-soft by local standards. It smells of road dust and relief.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Split logs worn smooth by sitting. The best arguments of the settlement happen here, and one or two of the marriages.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A domed clay oven with a stone apron swept twice a day, standing where the fire used to be. What comes out of it is the thing strangers end up describing when they try to say where they have been.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: An uncut stone with a cup-shaped hollow worn into its crown. Whatever is poured there is gone by morning, and no one asks where.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A cairn of fieldstone, raised for someone the settlement has not yet lost. It waits.

part.Name: RulesDescription
part.Text: The lower stones record the first claim: water found, ground kept, and one place promised to the dead. A blank capstone waits for the next name.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A low marker raised where the settlement named its first dead founder and passed the charter on.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A stone table with a gutter cut down the middle of it. What comes off a body here is read before it is cut, and written down.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Brine, tallow, and a shelf of things kept longer than anything ought to keep. Nothing here rots; that is the point of it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A lamp over a table, and somebody who has done this before. It does not sell augmentation. It performs it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Tiered seats around a table nobody sits at. This city is about one thing, and this is the thing.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A clean white room, a chair with restraints nobody has ever needed, and a book nobody else may read. The machines do not ask who your parents were. They ask the book.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A protected bore head stands inside a stone service hall, with the spoil lane and drainage kept clear. It works only when its reciprocal receipt is invoked.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A stone fire hall encloses the casting floor; worked metal belongs to its machines, never its shell. It works only when its reciprocal receipt is invoked.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Raised timber stores overlook a crop court and threshing floor. Its small measure of metal lives in gearing and fasteners, and its reciprocal work is always deliberate.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Four stilling bays face one clean transfer room, a custody desk, and a locker for effects. The vault is not an operating theatre: a body must leave stasis before anyone works on it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A worked-metal cradle, restraint-free and scrubbed bare. Its stilling interlock is a socket awaiting an authority, not a field that starts itself.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Crystals involute along angles of stillness around an empty power socket. It projects nothing by itself.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: An open circuit of witness seats and faceted chimes gathers around one consent focus. It is a congregation shaped by the Moon Stair, not a norm core disguised as a shrine.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Marble was faceted after Chavvah's chiming rock: an echo made by hands, not a stolen living branch. It rings only when struck.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A diamond-shaped manifold braces a circle of sockets, one for every assenting voice. It owns no reactor, field, vapor, deployment, or power switch.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: One room, and everything in it points at the middle of it. The floor was levelled by people who knew what would stand on it. Whatever else the kingdom argues about, it does not argue about where this is.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: One monumental shell closes around the capital's old court and opens into three parasang-wide storeys. Old marble survives at the civic centre; ceramic cultivation galleries rise above it, while numbered concrete service bays descend below. Every paid work still names the exact root that owns it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A catalogue witness for the materials and labour of one sealed lodging floor. The paid rooms themselves rise only inside the capital's exact hosted shell.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A catalogue witness for sealed growbeds, lamp rails, and fresh-water risers. Its food support exists only after those paid fixtures are active inside the hosted shell and the capital stores fresh water.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Broad concrete treads climb beside a sleeved cable well. The paired landing is cut to the same coordinate on the storey above.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Broad concrete treads descend beside a sleeved cable well. The paired landing is cut to the same coordinate on the storey below.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A numbered ring of salvaged metal marks where one sealed district opens into the next. Floor seams and sightlines continue exactly across the boundary.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The chrome platform's return plate names the exact shell that carries this interior.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Names, receipts, and remaining labour are cut into a bounded slate. It promises no work that the loaded capital cannot prove.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Old water-right marks survive on the rim. The dry stone basin is public history and architecture, not a second hidden water store.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A shallow ceramic bed sits under a salvaged spectrum lamp. Its crop is an architectural witness; the realm's food tally is derived only from the active hosted receipt and fresh-water stores.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A ceramic-jacketed riser carries only the water admitted by the capital's ordinary stores. There is no private reservoir behind the gauge.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Glazed pipe branches toward the growbeds. Chalk marks assign each run to one paid terrace receipt.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A glazed trough and dry lamp bracket show where a cultivation crew would work. It grows nothing and supports no tally without a paid terrace receipt.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Salvaged lenses are ranked above a disconnected ceramic bus. Ambient civic light catches their colours, but this rail generates and transmits no power.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A numbered cabinet face records nursery lineages. Its drawers are welded shut; it contains and stores nothing.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Ceramic fins surround an empty, disconnected jacket. The shell marks climate work but contains no water and produces none.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Scored ceramic gives a nursery crew a clean working height. The stand is bare and creates no crop or material.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Slatted ceramic shelves leave room for air around a future harvest. Nothing is stored, supplied, or dried here now.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A tiled range defines the public kitchen, scrubbed bare and cold. It cooks no meal and consumes no fuel.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A washable frame marks an examination bay. Without bedding or a ward receipt it is not a civic bed.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A communal washing bay slopes toward a disconnected drain. It has no liquid volume and creates no water.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A numbered metal frame awaits a sling and a named occupant. It is not a bed and grants no shelter capacity.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A painted line and bolted seat name a watch station. No guard is conjured to fill it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Numbered panels and relay diagrams identify a service bay. The cabinet has no inventory and supplies no parts.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A low numbered pallet reserves turning room beside the freight walk. It carries and stores nothing.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A bank of replaceable-filter doors marks the sanitation works. No fan turns, no charge moves, and no resource is produced.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A scarred metal worktop defines a repair bay. It contains no tools and performs no fabrication.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A stone table with a gutter cut in it, brine in the jars behind, and a hook by the door. What is dragged home here becomes parts and is kept. What happens to parts afterwards happens somewhere else.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A desk, a lamp, a clerk, and a copy of a book kept somewhere else. You may read who the realm counts. You may not become one of them at this desk.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A room taken out of the rock in an afternoon, because three of its four walls were already standing. The chisel marks are left where they fell; nobody here has ever pretended this was masonry.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Cells cut off one stair, each with a curtain and a shelf, and a door at the top that shuts against the cold coming up. Nothing here was carried down but the door.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Spawn pressed into damp cut rock and left alone in the dark, which is the heart of the method. One keeper goes down to scrape, inoculate, and wet the beds; the vault needs no lamp and keeps no surface season.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The whole run worked, propped and kept wet, with beds to the reach of either hand and a walkway down the middle that is slick no matter what is laid on it. No lamp is kept here; the spawn wants the dark.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A working face with props to the roof and the spoil going straight back into the wall behind it. The one yard in the settlement that will never run out of what it works.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A niche cut in the gallery wall for somebody the settlement has not yet lost, and a name cut under it. There is no field to gather stone from. There is this wall.

part.Name: RulesDescription
part.Text: The first line names the gallery and the hands that opened it. Beneath, an empty line reserves one death, one remembered deed, and no title greater than either.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A collared shaft, a windlass over it, and a rope going down further than the lamp reaches. The settlement owned the rock before this. Now it can get to it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A salvaged cradle of chrome and gut-wire, cranked by whoever has the shift. Set your cells on it and go eat; they will be full when you come back.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A small stone marker, plain and unlettered. It says nothing about what stands around it - only that the keepers looked, and it was satisfied.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Cut thornbrush lashed between stakes, taller than a man and meaner. It will not stop anyone determined. It will slow them down where your people can see them.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A platform on four legs with a bell and a good view of the road. The watch complains about the wind and never once about the posting.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Fieldstone laid without mortar, wide enough at the base to stand on. It took a season and everyone's back, and it will outlast everyone who built it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A thin codex in a plain wrapper, copied and recopied by people who had reason to. The margins argue with the text.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Hammered from tin and older promises, it holds just enough water to make strangers into kin. Whoever fills it and pours may found a place worth thirsting for.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A millstone yoked to a walking-bar. Three settlers lean into it from first light and spell each other at noon, and the shaft they turn runs under the packed floor to wherever the settlement wants the charge.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Paddles the settlement cut and lashed itself, standing in a race they dug under it and lined with clay. Nobody drinks out of that race. Somebody greases the shaft each morning and pulls the weed off the buckets. That is the whole of the work, and it is somebody's.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Four arms of brined wood and patched sailcloth on a post, trimmed by whoever draws the shift. On a still day it stands there being a landmark, and the settlement finds other work for the hands.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A jacketed pit of salt kept molten by the day's work and tapped after dark. The salt was already here. It is the one thing this country has never been short of.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Two rings of bone-pale marble set one inside the other and turned a quarter apart, standing on a floor the masons levelled twice and then levelled again. Between them the air holds still. While the works are paying for it there is a street in there, and it is not this one.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A bored log collared in salvaged tubing, laid in a shallow trench and packed over. Its fitting keeps a frozen set of joined faces; it joins only a neighbour that declares back.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The same trench and collar, marked by a double rule and carrying the other thing this country has never lacked. It refuses a fresh main by name rather than quietly making both brine.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: One trench crossing another with a hand's breadth of packed clay between them. The single and double rules show which opposite pair bears fresh water and which bears brine; the two never meet.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Where the main meets a vessel. Its fitting keeps a frozen set of joined faces; standing near a cistern joins nothing to it, and that difference is the whole of the law.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The same fitting on the double-ruled line. Put it on a fresh cistern and it refuses by name; that refusal tells the truth rather than making you brine.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Turned earth, wetted and trodden until it holds a shape. The cheapest wall anybody ever built, and the first one.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Cut scrub, bound and left to ret. It becomes cord, thatch, and the canvas a tent is made of, and it is the reason a roof can go up in an afternoon.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A trunk stripped, squared, and stacked to season. Somebody spent a day on this with an axe.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Shale or limestone, split along the grain and dressed square. It was a hillside this morning.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Snails and coral on the geologic press, cut out of a seam somebody found and will not stop talking about.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Squared, planed, and true on every face. Half the trunk it came from went out of the saw-pit as dust.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Squared on the banker until every face meets every other at a right angle. It will sit where it is put for a thousand years.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Ruin-scrap taken back to liquid and poured into a mould. Somebody read the colour of the melt and knew when to tap it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A line of pegs and a cord, and a mark cut into the nearest thing still standing. Everything inside the cord is coming down, and the settlement will be the richer for it.

part.Name: Chat
part.Says: [a tally of what stands here, and what it is worth once it does not.]

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Bare, level ground inside a staked square. Whatever stood here came down; whatever rises next can rise here again.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A notice on a stake, promising fresh water to whoever does what it asks.

part.Name: Chat
part.Says: [the price, and what it is for.]

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A short stake and a strip of cloth, the kind porters are trained to look for. Plant it on what you mean to have carried home, and walk on.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Pressed out of a windfall and dried on a cloth, still faintly sweet where the juice caught. Every one of them is a tree that has not happened yet.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Salt-crusted heads cut off a vine that had finished with them. They rattle. Put them in wet ground and stand back a week.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Damp grain run through with white thread, packed in a twist of bark. Not a seed at all, strictly; the people who sell it have never cared about the distinction.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A pressed disc of spore and ash the colour of something Qud has no word for. It is warm, and it should not be.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Knuckled lengths of starbright rhizome hum against one another in the packet. Cut into crystal loam, each keeps enough of its old rhythm to root again.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Cut tops of tubers, each with a bud on it and a low note under it you feel in the jaw. Whoever cut them wore gloves and did not linger.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Caps quartered and drowned in brine that went the wrong colour on the second day and has stayed that way. It keeps for years. Nobody has established why.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Boiled twice, drained twice, and pounded flat by somebody who wanted the job over with. Whatever is in a dreadroot that makes you afraid is mostly in the water they threw away.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A young tree in a line of young trees, staked against a wind that has opinions. In a week there will be light in the branches.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Vine trained along a stake, its furrows still empty of salt. Somebody walks this row every morning with a bucket.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A raised bed of spent grain and shade, threaded white where the spawn took. It smells like rain in a cellar.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Spore-cake worked into cool soil and left alone. The keepers will not say what colour it comes up; the ones who have seen it do not have the word.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Woody blades grow in a scored line through crystal loam. Their notes interfere until the whole row sounds like rain heard through stone.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Shoots in a line, and under each one a swelling belly of tuber. Nobody sings while they weed this row.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Bricks dug out of the pan, moulded in a frame, and left in the flat sun until they ring. Cool at noon, warm at midnight, and nothing in it ever grew.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The hut, a wall around a square of swept pan, and a strip of shade along its north side that the whole street borrows in the afternoon.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A blank wall to the wind, one gate wide enough for a laden pack-dromad, and a yard of stalls around a trough. Nobody who outspans here leaves without having argued about the price of salt.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Posts driven into the silt, a plank walk between the doors, and standing water underneath that nobody pretends is going away. The floor stays dry. That is the whole ambition.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A sapling planted for somebody the settlement has not yet lost, and a name cut into the stake beside it. There is no fieldstone here. There is this.

part.Name: RulesDescription
part.Text: Each stake begins blank. When a settler dies, their name and one remembered deed are cut before the sapling is tied upright.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Cut down into cold earth and shut with a stone lid, because a granary standing in the open under this canopy is a granary full of somebody else's crop by spring.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A dwelling cut under a living cap and left unlit, because the people who ask for one are the people a lamp keeps awake. Water beads on the gills all night and runs down the inside of the wall, and to the right tenant that is the whole selling point.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Canvas is tensioned between pale ribs cut to follow the local crystal, all of it set on a black marble sill. The folded walls shed warm-static drizzle and leave the doorway open to the noisegrass.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Black marble walks circle clear basins and young crystal roots. Their facets scatter the Moon Stair's restless sky into slow bands that cross the court as people gather.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A young hexagonal root was left standing when the court was cut around it. Footfall sends pale pulses through its buried lattice.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A pale root was left standing, dressed only where cord crosses its facets. Canvas strains between it and its twin when warm static walks the Stair.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A fallen course of fulcrete squared off, roofed in salvaged plate, and lived in. The ancients cut the hard part; somebody swept it out.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Two courses re-stood at a right angle and the corner between them swept, walled with plate, and used. The yard was a room once. Nobody knows whose.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The wall that was already here, put back up. Half of it is still the original mortar and the other half is whatever came to hand, and from outside you cannot tell which half is which.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Lamps strung low over a bench that was a bulkhead, and a rule pinned above it that the ancients were not gods and did not leave a note. Everything here comes apart before it goes together.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: One machine, cased, lit, and not repaired. It has not run in the memory of anyone here and that is not the point; the point is that it was made, and that making is holy.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A counting room, a strongbox, and a ledger of what every cask in this settlement is worth today against what it was worth last season. Water is money and this is where the money is written down.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Apple pips and watervine cuttings lie in separate cool bins, each marked with the season and the field that bore it. Joppa survives by knowing what to put back in the earth.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A low smoking hearth stands between drying screens and stoppered jars. Nothing here is merely stored; smoke, brine, and good leaf turn one harvest into another season's suppers.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A spindle turns beneath a broad shade while fibre dries on curved racks. The wheel is small, but every hand at it learns the patient lesson of the great tree.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Low hide screens shelter spoor boards and butchered trail meat. Every passage bends toward open ground; nobody who keeps watch here agrees to be cornered.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Warm slabs are set far enough apart for a great mineral body to rest among them. Their courses carry footsteps through the ground long before a voice reaches the court.

part.Name: RulesDescription
part.Text: Each slab records one arrival by its weight and bearing, not a written name. A listener at the centre reads the settlement's history through the order of the stones.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Dry contacts run beside a grounded turning rail. The bay is built to admit a metal body, service it without ceremony, and send it back out under its own charge.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The old dry contacts remain where robot feet learned them. Dressed flooring, labelled parts drawers, and a shielded inspection light make the same bay fit for sustained service without inventing a second source of charge.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A measured gantry holds requested objects on one side and recorded answers on the other. The empty centre belongs to the baetyl, whether one is present or not.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A broad awning covers sample racks, water measures, and enough turning room for a laden beast. No wall closes the road; a market that cannot leave is only a storehouse.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Offset stone and cloth baffles surround a witness plate scored by warm static. The arrangement does not master disorder. It lets careful minds stand near it long enough to write.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Horn posts mark a ring whose centre remains bare for challenge, dancing, and judgment. A decision made here has been heard from every side before it leaves.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Shallow cool basins join through a wet crawl, with feeding shelves kept just above the waterline. It is nursery, pantry, and comfortable ground to bodies the dry air punishes.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Bright fragments are wired around a guarded niche, not repaired and not mistaken for refuse. Offerings enter by the narrow way and leave, if they leave, under witness.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Three heavy spans meet at a toll-stone. Each will bear a troll's weight, and each forces a visitor to choose which approach they mean before they reach the middle.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A shaded rest braces a long gun toward the road. Its flanks are screened against glare and gossip alike; the one clear sightline is the one that matters.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Two private alcoves share a small vestibule and no register. The door keeps weather out, asks no name, and opens back onto the road without passing another bed.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Pale stones ring a clear place for dancing, testimony, and judgment beneath the moon. The entries face one another so nobody takes the court without being seen.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Two hearths crouch behind a windbreak, one cooking while the other keeps yesterday's pot warm. The serving gap faces inward, where a hidden camp becomes a household.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Six dressed drains descend toward a vessel sealed in old metal. What gathers there is kept as sacrament and specimen together, and the dry walk never crosses its course.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Whitewashed racks stand behind one narrow inspection lane. Arms pass from unclean entry to ordered issue without either path touching the other.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A crooked procession winds among four cold braziers and returns nowhere near where it began. Ash marks the path more reliably than stone.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A red-sealed basin lies beyond a counting shelf and below a dry witness step. The gift descends. The record does not.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Thick stone and hanging cloth baffles turn every passage before it reaches one unadorned seat. A mind working here hears itself before it hears the street.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A public bench faces the visitor while a clear side passage faces the road. Hospitality and vigilance occupy the same room without pretending to be the same duty.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Sealed measures hang beside witness marks cut into stone. The sluice has one lock, the register has another, and neither can be opened unseen from the gauging step.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Two scales face a public price board while three seals wait at the clerk's table. Buyer, seller, and guild can each see where a measure changed hands.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Labelled bins surround a threshing floor held in common. Seed enters by crop and season, and leaves only after the next field has been named.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Clean pallets face an open basin and no door is barred. The room is ordered for tending rather than worship, which is how its devotion is shown.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Broken tools enter at the stripping bench, cross a rack of named parts, and leave by the fitting bench. The route teaches repair by making every failure visible.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Fruiting trellises turn around a table left open to travellers. Shade, food, and talk arrive by the same paths and none is kept behind a wall.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Low desks stand in living shade, every aisle curving around the trunk at the centre. Teaching bends to the life already there instead of cutting through it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A witnessed demand carried from a named grievance. Its marks mean nothing without the living incident recorded behind them.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Salt-stiff cord knots hide tabs, tooth nicks, and one red thread into a snapjaw road-claim. Reading it means acknowledging the demand; carrying it keeps the answer-road open.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Barkcloth bears ranked tooth marks and a charcoal path-sign. The troop's grievance can be answered wherever this exact writ is carried.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Cured hide is scored in the cadence of distant war-horns and sealed with a horn shaving. It names water, ground, and the band expecting an answer.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A thin bone tally is wrapped in roadcloth, its cuts matched by a short inked demand. It is unpleasant, legible, and exact.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A clean strip of riflecloth carries a measured desert claim in oil-black script. The answering terms are aligned like sights along its edge.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A veined-marble cabinet keeps folded blankets, scented rushes, and the small comforts of a quiet house behind fitted doors. Even shut, its deep drawers soften the room's clatter.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Marble-fronted drawers and a broad service ledge hold the linens, cups, and guest goods of a manor. Everything has a handsome place, and nothing need trouble the household's welcome.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: This dressed-stone cabinet has shallow cupboards on both faces so court attendants can serve a gathering without crossing it. Its polished ledge bears the scratches of many shared cups.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A lashed-timber cradle hangs between the stilt-house joists, where a sealed vessel can cool the boards above. It is empty when raised and lends damp only while it holds real fresh water.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A ribbed timber cradle nestles under the living cap, catching its cool shade around a stoppered water vessel. Construction leaves it empty; fresh water must be kept inside before the room grows damp.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A low stone coffer waits behind the guest screen with a cup, a folded wrap, and room for a traveller's dust-stained things. Its worn lid serves as both welcome and bedside table.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A clean sheet of salvaged plate forms this tending station, with hooks for bandages and a shallow ledge for a healer's hands. A hospice tender works here beneath Resheph's remembered mercy.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Reclaimed metal has been scrubbed bright and folded into a washstand beside the hospice basin. It begins empty and serves only when a tender keeps a vessel of fresh water in it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Labelled drawers, rounded corners, and a wipe-clean counter make this worked-metal station fit for a crowded arcology ward. Bedclothes and common comforts remain close without choking the aisle.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Low fieldstone seats broaden the reservoir lip into a public promenade around its open bowl. The basin is dry at construction and becomes a cool gathering place only while it openly holds fresh water.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A public gauge rises from a dressed-stone plinth, its face broad enough to read across the waterworks floor. The smooth rim invites neighbours to linger and compare the day's measure.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A worked-metal gauge with a glassy sight tube shows each silver bead won from the air. Condensery hands keep its fittings bright, and onlookers gather to watch the measure climb.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A fieldstone trough cups loam beneath the fungal vault, scored with channels where wet roots may travel. It is dry and unsown when built; only the vault's deliberately sown root culture draws damp through it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Dressed-stone beds run beneath the gallery lights, their shallow runnels ready for a living fungal root. They begin unsown and dry, and yield damp only after the gallery's cultivation has taken root.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Salvaged plates and riveted ribs hold an open nursery pool sized for sVardym young. The basin is empty when installed; only a standing fill of true, non-fresh brine makes the habitat live.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Hammered scrap encloses a sealed vessel beneath the rot-chapel's witness marks. A keeper of the Girsh rite tends it, reading instruction in what softens, blooms, and returns.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A scrap-bound offal vessel squats under the chapel seal, its joints packed against seepage. It is empty at construction and grows wet only when real corpse-stock and liquid are kept together within.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Witness cuts crowd the brass, wire, and salvaged plate of this Water-Baron gauge. A sworn reader compares its line before the gauge-house company and makes the measure public.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A sealed scrap-metal well feeds the Water-Baron gauge through a narrow sight tube. It starts empty and speaks true only while fresh water rests inside and a sworn reader attends it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A plated grading table is pierced with measured sieves and bordered by bins for seed, fibre, and spoil. Farm hands sort the home plots' harvest here before anything reaches a storehouse.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: The timber top is dark with oil and crosshatched by years of sharpening. Pegs, wedges, and a straight working edge make this modest bench the place where hand tools return to readiness.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A salvaged flywheel, braided wire, and a long hand crank turn patient muscle into a little charge. A post keeper braces the frame and works the handle through its heavy stroke.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: This broad fieldstone has been chosen for a level face and the clean ring it gives beneath a hammer. A smith works hot metal across its blackened crown without pretending it is finer than stone.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A dense stone block bears a dressed striking face, hardy enough for the forge's longer heats. Hammer scars overlap like scales where a practiced smith draws and turns the work.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Worked plate encloses a deep refractory bed whose heat can be banked between shifts. Forge-hall hands feed the draught, rake the coals, and bring billets to an even glow.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A massive worked-metal anvil stands beside the casting floor, with hardy corners for gates, sprues, and cooled seams. Foundry hands turn each piece over its face before it leaves the hall.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Two local stones meet along a patient, pecked face, the upper one notched for a grain hopper and turning staff. Mill hands keep the feed even while flour gathers around the curb.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Recovered plate caps this scarred workshop bench, while drawers of wire, fasteners, and curious fragments sit below. A craftsperson can test an idea here and leave its lesson visible in the work.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Paired fieldstone sleepers hold a timber crossbar steady above the saw pit. Sawyers roll a trunk onto the notches and work along a clear, dangerous line.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A waist-high banker of fitted stone presents one true edge and one sacrificial face. Masons dress blocks upon it, letting chips fall into the yard instead of underfoot indoors.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Salvaged plate cinches a clay-lined furnace around a narrow firebox and tapping mouth. Smelter hands judge the heat, skim the dross, and draw useful metal from the charge.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Charred stakes and laid fuelwood mark a communal fire kept for pot, story, and shared observance. Its hearth gives neighbours one warm centre at which to cook and remember together.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A low stone oven cups heat behind a soot-dark mouth and broad baking ledge. Bread, roots, and festival dishes pass through the same warmth, making ordinary cooking a communal rite.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Two worn timber seats face one another across a deliberate handspan. Under an appointed moderator, neighbours sit here until a grievance has words, witnesses, and an answer.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A stone stand lifts the settlement charter above the moot floor, its reading face angled toward every seat. The speaker keeps one hand on the text while memory and judgment contend around it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A long stone counter bears tally grooves, cup rings, and a trader's honest working edge. Market hands weigh, reckon, and exchange goods across it beneath the noise of the bazaar.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Dressed stone forms a deep public bath with broad steps and a ledge for the bath keeper's jars. It is dry when completed and welcomes bathers only with real fresh water and an attendant at work.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: This unadorned fieldstone stands beside the first basin, polished where founding hands laid witness upon it. Its place, more than its shape, remembers the city's first drink together.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A fitted stone plinth keeps the retained first basin visible above the changed heart around it. Witnesses gather here to name old water, new obligations, and the city that joins them.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Joined timbers rise into a speaking platform built through the old heart rather than merely beside it. A moot keeper faces the gathered city here while the founding ground remains underfoot.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Worked-metal steps and a resonant speaking rail crown the transformed civic heart. From this rostrum, an appointed voice can address the whole great court and answer before it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A palm-sized stone cup rests before the shrine, darkened by water, oil, ash, and the touch of petitioners. Each offering makes devotion tangible upon the open garth.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A low stone table gathers cups, keepsakes, and weathered tokens within the shrine-garth. Rain and dust share its surface with whatever worshippers choose to leave.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A dressed-stone lectern stands in the temple's lit sanctum, its face broad enough for text, relic, or teaching object. A temple keeper reads and interprets before the assembled seats.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A carved stone desk resists spilled ink beneath a sloped copying face and shallow tool wells. Scribes compare texts here, preserving a lesson while questioning every uncertain line.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A board of salvaged plate carries patrol pegs, route scratches, and a place for each watcher's mark. The watch keeper musters the shift here before anyone takes the road.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Joined timber boards divide the barracks roster by squad, watch, and duty. An officer moves the pegs at muster, making absence and readiness plain to every bunk.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Local stones rise in a hand-built cairn, each one chosen or carried by somebody who remembers. The names may fade, but the settlement still walks around the weight of its dead.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A worn timber walking bar turns the mill through a stout central socket. Millers lean into its circle together, trading footsteps for meal and flour.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Recovered bearings and a riveted drive head take the waterwheel's slow force from the millrace. A mill hand watches the shudder of the shaft and keeps its teeth engaged.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A salvaged bearing carries the sail-vane above a braced yard frame. Its keeper trims the sweep into the wind and listens for the scrape that foretells a failed race.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A carved stone casing channels salt into a dry collecting throat around a buried charge sink. The accumulator works only while its capacitor holds power; dark stone gathers nothing.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A salvaged treadle stitcher braces a scratched metal C around needle and bobbin, while a foot bar drives each lockstitch. Hindren clothiers teach repair, cutting, and remembered patterns beside it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A broad stone counter gives caravan masters room for ledgers, cups, seals, and disputed bundles. The house factor receives travellers here and witnesses what enters or leaves the court.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A living memorial tree has been trained around a low timber rail, with names cut where bark will slowly fold over them. Root and remembrance deepen together in the grave-grove soil.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Black marble rims a civic basin beneath branching crystal, giving every side an equal place to gather. It is dry when finished; fresh water in the bowl turns the crystal court into a cool meeting ground.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Fieldstone props bite into the opened deep-cut, holding back loose layers around a clear working face. Miners sound each brace before striking where the assigned cut continues.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A memorial niche is cut directly into dressed gallery stone, just deep enough for a name and a few retained things. Lamp smoke gathers above the carving while footsteps pass below.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A dressed-stone workface runs over fitted parts lockers beneath the underbench. Delvers sort recovered mechanisms here, learning their joins before returning anything to use.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Dressed stone embraces a retained machine without disguising its impossible seams. The reliquary asks visitors to witness the old device as it stands, half lesson and half holy object.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A marble ledger desk presents a polished public face and a deep, lockable factor's drawer. Goods, promises, and caravan marks become one witnessed reckoning across its top.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A stone board beside the Kyakukyan hearth is stained gold, red, and green by generations of crushed spice. Hearth keepers grind, mix, and teach the fragrant order of each shared dish.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A hand-cut stone bearing steadies Ezra's spindle wheel beneath its shade. A practiced spinner turns local fibre into even thread while explaining every adjustment to waiting learners.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: This cragmensch-sized slab was chosen for the long, low note it returns through the stone garden. Those who sit against it listen through back and bone as much as through ears.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A grounded rail of salvaged contacts runs the length of the robot charge-bay. Bay hands brace a chassis against it, clear corrosion, and keep each charging berth aligned.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A dressed-stone inspection rail holds a robot level above the service trench, with shallow lockers close at hand. Mechanics work along its whole length without crowding the machine's joints.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Salvaged struts hold tablets and answer marks around the baetyl's audience ground. An attendant records each demand exactly, because a baetyl's words tolerate neither ornament nor convenient memory.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A public stone measure stands under the dromad shade, worn smooth by water vessels and trade weights. A caravan factor works in full view so guest and host share the same reckoning.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A salvaged metal plate is scored with reference lines and set where the blind's basin can cast its changing signs. A patient observer records each deviation and teaches others how to doubt the pattern.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A tall stone standard closes the goatfolk challenge ring, with notches for horns, names, and settled claims. A ring keeper calls each contest from its foot and remembers the result.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: An altar of welded scrap presents its guarded face beneath Naphtaali tokens and hard-won adornments. A keeper receives offerings here while armed witnesses ring the court.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A blunt toll-stone stands where three bridge approaches become one question. Its troll keeper names the price, hears the traveller's answer, and lets the crossing remember both.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A long stone rest fixes the Issachari porch's view down a single open lane. A watch shooter settles a rifle here and scans the salt beyond without wavering the barrel.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Pale marble catches the night above the Hindren court, its face divided by old judgment cuts. Under moonlight, speakers stand beside it while the gathered kin weigh word against memory.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A broad stone board bridges the space between the Mopango refuge's paired hearths. Kitchen hands portion each pot here so shelter, warmth, and supper follow one visible order.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Straight bars of salvaged metal divide this Putus Templar rack by weapon, rank, and inspection mark. An arsenal keeper checks every empty hook before the company is dismissed.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A dark stone standard rises among braziers of sifted ash, its grooves grey with repeated handling. Gyre Wight keepers gather at it to witness what the Gyre took and what still endures.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Hammered scrap forms a shallow basin beneath Mamon's tally shelves, its rim bright where offerings pass. A tithe keeper displays each gift before lowering it into the cistern court's custody.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A stone seat faces the quiet cell's bare listening wall, shaped to keep the body still through a long vigil. A Seeker attends the listener and gives disciplined inquiry a place to begin.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Porous stone panels interlock across the Seeker cell, breaking echoes into a hush without sealing out the world. Their angled faces make the fitted room measurably quieter.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A salvaged sighting post aligns the lodge window, watch bench, and road beyond. A warden checks the same narrow line at every change of watch and records what crosses it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A beam scale balances on a stone pier in the middle of the weighing house. Merchant witnesses set both goods and counterweights in public, where no sleeve can hide the measure.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A salvaged-metal bench leaves its clamps, parts trays, and mistakes open to view. A Daughter of Exile repairs at one side while learners repeat the work at the other.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A low stone table rests under the Yd Freehold's living vine bower, cool even at salt-noon. A host pours for travellers here while tendrils knot themselves through the trellis overhead.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A stone writing ledge follows the living curve of Chavvah's bough without biting into its bark. Teacher and learners gather around the trunk, sharing questions beneath the leaves.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A dense stone slab slopes toward a catch groove, with basket room kept clear at the working end. The butcher dresses carcasses here under steady hands and an easily washed edge.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A dressed-stone table sets knives, seals, and preserving jars in a clean line between the vat-house vessels. Its keeper prepares each cut before it enters long storage.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A dressed-stone vat is sealed around a deep preserved-stock chamber. It is empty when built and supplies wet offal only while real corpse-stock remains immersed in liquid inside.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Worked metal forms a narrow procedure table with drains, restraint points, and labelled instrument ledges. A trained grafting crew works here where every cut and join can be reached.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A plated cabinet seals the grafting hall's preserved tissue behind lipped shelves. Construction leaves it empty; only real corpse-stock stored together with liquid gives the hall wet offal.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A seamless metal table branches into articulated rests for bodies that may not keep one familiar shape. Theatre specialists set tools and limbs within reach before the chimeric work begins.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Worked plate encloses a deep vat beside the chimeric theatre, with clamps sized for an uneasy variety of stock. It begins empty and provides wet offal only when corpse-stock stands in liquid within.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A worked-metal chair locks into the annexe floor beneath a halo of adjustable restraints and contact arms. Becoming attendants inspect every joint before seating anyone at its centre.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Worked-metal induction coils cradle cells and devices beside the becoming chair. Newly installed, its capacitor is dark; once supplied with charge, its real contacts can replenish what rests there.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A worked-metal cutting head coils heavy teeth around a socket built for the great bore. Bore crews gauge its edges and keep it ready beside the machine that will bear its weight.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Layered metal and refractory brick form a forge broad enough for realm-scale castings. Foundry crews bank its heat in shifts, never leaving the bright mouth unwatched.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: This worked-metal casting anvil spreads its mass through the foundry floor on branching feet. Crews dress gates, seams, and stubborn flaws across different faces of the same block.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A plated furnace climbs around a refractory shaft, feeding molten wealth toward the great foundry's casting floor. Its crew reads heat and flow through shielded ports before opening the tap.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A worked-metal ledger desk faces the colossus controls, its drawers divided by settlement, season, and seal. Granary officers reconcile every great movement of stores beneath the machine's shadow.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A worked-metal keying core rests cold between the mirror-gate lights. It is unpaired when built and wakes only when both keyed arches form a powered reciprocal link.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Worked-metal steps lift a witness chair into the crown hall's full view, with no screen between ruler and assembly. Heralds and petitioners meet the seated crown across this accountable distance.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A sleek metal dais bends one council table around the arcology's central speaking place. Assigned councillors work face to face while the surrounding galleries look inward.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A dressed-stone procedure slab stands under the hall surgery's best light, cut with drains and reachable tool ledges. The surgery staff works around all four sides without blocking the ward aisle.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A fitted stone vat closes beneath the hall surgery's preserved-stock shelves. It is empty on construction and provides wet offal only while corpse-stock and liquid are actually held together inside.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A dressed stone desk joins witness shelf, seal well, and writing face into one public station. The registrar records names and obligations here while their witnesses still stand close enough to object.
